title: Sleep Like a Pokemon in Japan's Poke Ball Hotel
paragraphs: Have you ever wanted to sleep inside a Poké Ball? In October 2026, a small number of lucky Pokémon fans in Japan were able to do just that.

The Poké Ball hotel was built in Tomakomai, Hokkaido, next to a lake. It was created by the Japanese company NOT A HOTEL for The Pokémon Company. It was part of a campaign to celebrate the third anniversary of Pokémon Sleep, a smartphone app that tracks how people sleep, and the 30th anniversary of Pokémon.

The hotel is a ball that is three meters wide, and it looks just like a Poké Ball from the games. Inside, there is a round bed with a special round mattress. Guests can look at the scenery of Hokkaido from their bed through a large curved window. The bathroom has tiles in the colors of Snorlax, a sleepy Pokémon. Guests can also choose their favorite Pokémon on a tablet, and when the lights go off, the room is filled with lights connected to that Pokémon.

However, people could not book a room at the hotel. Instead, fans had to enter a competition on the social media site X in September 2026. Only 10 pairs of winners, or 20 people in total, were chosen to stay for one night between October 8 and 18. The stay was free, and it included dinner and breakfast, but winners had to pay to travel to Hokkaido. Only people living in Japan could enter.
Everyone who entered the competition received a code for an item in the Pokémon Sleep game.
The hotel was only for a limited time, and there are no plans to open it to the public.
